caption:
9 deaths in 24 hours. A record number of hospitalisations. Dengue is hitting Bangladesh hard.

According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), 9 people died from dengue in the last 24 hours, marking the highest single-day death toll of the year.

A record 1,571 patients were admitted to hospitals within the same period, surpassing the previous single-day high of 1,558 recorded last Sunday.

This brings the total number of dengue deaths this year to 130, with 45,475 total hospitalisations reported so far.

In Dhaka, 196 patients were admitted to hospitals in the North City Corporation area and 134 in the South City Corporation area, while 408 more were admitted in the Dhaka division outside the city.

Other affected regions include Khulna with 242 admissions, Barishal with 142, Chattogram with 117, Mymensingh with 77, Rangpur with 71, Rajshahi with 116, and Sylhet with 8.

The Khulna division has reported the highest total number of patients so far, with 7,298 cases.

For historical context, 400 people died from dengue last year, and approximately 102,000 were identified as patients.

The most severe outbreak occurred in 2023, when 1,705 people died and 321,179 were admitted to hospitals, the highest in 23 years.

headline_marked: Actress Azmeri Haque Badhan [[attacked in Venice]] by miscreants
headline: Actress Azmeri Haque Badhan attacked in Venice by miscreants
summary: The actress and her family, including a child, were harassed and pelted with eggs and water while attending the Venice International Film Festival.
details: Actress Azmeri Haque Badhan and her family were harassed and attacked by a group of miscreants in Venice, Italy, while attending the Venice International Film Festival.

The attackers pelted them with carbonated water and eggs, knocking off Badhan's phone and spectacles. The group reportedly forced them to chant 'Joy Bangla' and targeted her for her political views during the July 2024 protests.
Badhan, who describes herself as a 'July Warrior', stated that she remains unshaken and vowed that she would not be silenced. She recorded the incident to expose the attackers.
The attack has sparked outrage in Bangladesh's cultural circle, with fellow artists and directors calling for a fair trial and justice for the actress.
The incident was raised in the the Bangladesh Parliament, where Deputy Speaker Barrister Kayser Kamal denounced the attack as an 'inhuman, cowardly attack'.
The Bangladesh government, through the Foreign Ministry and the Consulate in Milan, has vowed to take legal action and provide all necessary support to the actress.
Badhan was in Venice for the premiere of the film 'The Difficult Bride', the first official Bangladeshi feature-length film selection for the Venice International Film Festival.
